screens.title: Main window
screens.purpose: The main window is the full Taskscape task-manager window. It composes the title bar, one task pane (or two in split view), an empty state when there are no lists, a right-hand aside that shows the preview/inspector panel (or the trash pane or filter panel), and app-wide overlays (command palette, sheet host, toast).

regions.name: window root
regions.contents: App root div (App.tsx:57), flex column, h-screen w-screen, overflow-hidden; wrapped by ContextMenuProvider (App.tsx:56, 146). 1180x760 in main-default, main-dark, split-view, preview-hidden and no-lists; 820x640 in narrow-window (footer at y 615-617).

regions.name: title bar
regions.contents: TitleBar at 0,0 1180x46 (820x46 in narrow-window). Holds window controls, drag grip, project switcher 'Home', list tabs 'Errands', 'Reading', 'Garden' (each with a delete-list button), the New list button, and the right-side toolbar (Split view, Swap panes in split view only, Hide/Show preview panel, Settings). Light grey surface in the light theme, dark in main-dark. Full detail is on the title-bar screen.

regions.name: body row
regions.contents: div flex min-h-0 flex-1 (App.tsx:60), y=46 to 761 in main-default. Places the task area and the right aside side by side.

regions.name: task area (left)
regions.contents: div flex min-w-0 flex-1 (App.tsx:62) when an active list exists. Holds the left TaskPane in a flexBasis slot (App.tsx:63-70; 100% alone, splitRatio*100% when split) and, when split, a Resizer and a second TaskPane slot (App.tsx:71-90). When no active list exists, EmptyState fills the area (App.tsx:92-106). Each pane has a search bar, task rows (y 98 to about 364 in main-default) and a StatsBar footer (y 729-760).

regions.name: search bar
regions.contents: Top of each pane, y 56-91 in main-default. Search field with leading search icon and placeholder 'Search Errands' (split right pane: 'Search Reading'), then Search options (tune) inside a ScopeFields wrapper, a vertical hairline divider, and New task (add). The split right pane also has a Close split button.

regions.name: task rows
regions.contents: Rows of 32 px (one-line), 46 px (two-line with subtitle) and 126 px (expanded parent with subtasks), with hairline dividers between rows. Each row: Select round checkbox, title, optional subtitle or subtask badge, More button. Completed rows have struck-through grey text.

regions.name: split divider
regions.contents: Resizer between the two task panes (App.tsx:73-85). Only present in split-view (state:split-view tree.txt:99, @430,46 4x715). Drag sets splitRatio clamped to 0.25 to 0.75; double-click resets it (App.tsx:78-84).

regions.name: right aside
regions.contents: Resizer (App.tsx:110-116) followed by aside with style width previewW, shrink-0, border-l (App.tsx:117-120). Rendered when previewOpen || trashOpen || filterOpen (App.tsx:108). Shows TrashPane if trashOpen, else FilterPanel if filterOpen, else PreviewPanel (App.tsx:121-131). Main-default: aside at 861,46 319x715, hairline at x about 860. Surface is a little darker in main-dark (not measured).

regions.name: empty list state
regions.contents: EmptyState in place of the task area when the active project has no lists (App.tsx:92-105). Shown only in no-lists, centred in the blank area (860x715 at y 46).

regions.name: overlays
regions.contents: Mounted at window-root level after the frame (App.tsx:138-145): CommandPalette when paletteOpen, SheetHost (always mounted), Toast (always mounted).

screens.title: Title bar
screens.purpose: The title bar is the 46px chrome band across the top of the main window. It holds the macOS window controls (leading), a drag grip, the project switcher pill (showing Home in the recordings), the per-project list tabs with a New list button, and a right-side toolbar with Split view, preview toggle and Settings. On Windows and Linux the window controls move to the trailing edge.

links.via: Single-click a task row (or its title area) to select it. The preview panel then shows its TaskInspector (state:row-selected, state:rename-inline, state:option-held-hover).

Cmd-click or Ctrl-click a row to add it to the selection, Shift-click for a range, or click the Check handle on rows. With one or more rows selected the footer becomes BulkBar and the preview shows MultiInspector (state:multi-select-shift).
Right-click a task row, or click its More (more_horiz) button. Shows the row context menu (single or multi variant).
Click the Search options (tune) button in the search bar. Shows the scope and fields menu.
Row context menu item 'Move to list' (submenu of list names), or BulkBar 'Move to…' (menu of other lists in the active project).
Click the Sort & filter (tune) button in the footer. Toggles the Filter & Sort panel.
Click the New task (add) button in the search bar, or press '+' or ⌘N (per the empty-state hint).
Row context menu 'Delete task…' or 'Delete {n} tasks…', or BulkBar 'Delete'. The confirmation sheet is inferred from requestDeleteTask and is not verified in the files read.
Empty-list subtitle text '⌘↩ anywhere to capture one' refers to the capture bar. This is text only in the code; the hotkey is toggle_capture_bar. Target inferred.

screens.title: Draft inspector
screens.purpose: The new-task draft shown in the right preview panel before any database row exists. The user types an optional title, or uses "Start with" Note / Screenshot to create the task as "Untitled" and add content; Escape, the Discard draft button, or a click-away with no title drops the draft and writes nothing.

screens.title: Multi-select inspector
screens.purpose: Multi-select inspector body in the preview panel, shown when the focused pane has more than one task selected. It shows a combined tally, bulk verbs (Done, Undone, Move, Copy, Delete), and a list of the selected tasks, where each row has a done checkbox, a title that peeks the task, a list-name badge, and an Open button that narrows the selection to that one task.

screens.title: Command palette
screens.purpose: The ⌘K command palette is a modal overlay over the main window that lets the user run any app command, or jump to a list in the active project or any project, by typing part of its label. Results are grouped under View, Task, Manage, Go to list and Go to project, and the list filters live as the user types.

regions.name: Scrim
regions.contents: Full-window dim layer at [0,0,1180,760]. Soft dim (background oklab(0 0 0 / 0.3)), no blur. Its className starts "px-space-8 flex items-start justify-center pt-[12vh] pb-[8vh…", so the panel sits near the top, centred horizontally. Mousedown outside the panel dismisses the palette. The main window is visible through it.

regions.name: Palette panel
regions.contents: Menu-elevation surface 2, panel radius, 490 px wide at x=345, top edge y=91. Height follows content: 456 px (palette), 184 px (palette-search), 109 px (palette-no-match). Max height 60vh, flex column, overflow hidden, animate-sheet-in. Contains the input row and the results list or the empty message. No footer, no close button, no hint bar.

regions.name: Input row
regions.contents: Header row, h-11 (44 px), shrink-0, flex, centred, gap-space-5, px-space-6, with a bottom border that acts as the divider under the input. Holds the bolt icon at 355,102 (18x18) and the command text input at 380,100 (446x21).

regions.name: Results list
regions.contents: Scrolling container (ref listRef), py-space-3, min-h-0, flex-1, overflow-y-auto. Palette state: 19 rows under 5 group headings (View, Task, Manage, Go to list, Go to project), content taller than the 60vh cap so it scrolls at some window sizes. Palette-search state (query "new"): 3 rows under 2 headings (Task, Manage). Keeps the active row in view with scrollIntoView block nearest.

regions.name: Empty state (palette-no-match)
regions.contents: Single centred message "No matching commands" in a box at [346,134,488,62] below the input row (query "zzzz"). No rows and no group headings.

widgets.behaviour: Dismiss (outside click or Escape, via onDismiss) calls onClose. Escape is captured by the overlay. Focus is trapped inside the palette.

widgets.purpose: Filter query for the command list. It is focused automatically on open.
widgets.text: Placeholder "Run a command or jump to…" (single ellipsis character). Typed values in reference states: "" (palette), "new" (palette-search), "zzzz" (palette-no-match).
widgets.behaviour: Typing sets q and resets the active row to 0. The list is filtered by case-insensitive substring match on the label (not fuzzy) and ranked by match index, earlier matches first, stable. areas.name: Command palette, menus, toast and sheets

screens.title: Menus
screens.purpose: Context and dropdown menus for the Taskscape desktop task manager: a single app-wide menu layer (ContextMenu with a ContextMenuProvider) that opens anchored at a pointer or button position for task rows, the list tab strip, and a project dropdown under the project switcher. Menu items are plain rows with an icon, a label, an optional shortcut and an optional submenu chevron, and the caller decides what each item id does.

regions.name: menu-layer
regions.contents: Overlay (layer="menu", placement="anchored", dim="none", captureEscape, dismissOnWindowChange) covering the full window 1180x760 (state boxes @0,0). Contains Backdrop2 (full-window, transparent, dismisses on mousedown and right-click) and, when a menu is open, one MenuPanel. Sits above the sheet layer (ContextMenu.tsx:30-32). Only rendered when a menu is open. Not present in the project-menu state.

regions.name: task-context-menu
regions.contents: Surface2 154x175 at the anchor point, rendered in states row-context-menu (@108,190), row-more-menu (@830,135) and multi-context-menu (@101,221). Rows, top to bottom: Copy (content_copy); divider; Add subtask (subdirectory_arrow_right); Rename (edit); Move to list (arrow_forward, submenu chevron_right); divider; Delete task… (delete, danger). Each row 152x30. Anchor variants: pointer (row-context-menu), More button (row-more-menu), and a single-row menu on Cut a spare key (multi-context-menu). No multi-selection is evidenced in the recording or in ContextMenu.tsx.

regions.name: tab-context-menu
regions.contents: Surface2 158x145 at @348,21 in state tab-context-menu, under the Reading list tab (x 322-376) in the ListTabs strip. Rows, top to bottom: Rename (edit); Open in split view (vertical_split, disabled=false); divider; Export list… (ios_share); divider; Delete list… (delete, danger). Each row 156x30. The menu covers only the top part (y 21-32) of the Reading tab close button (21x21 at 380,11). Its preview shows no task selected.

regions.name: project-dropdown
regions.contents: ProjectMenu Surface2 210x112 at @112,43 in state project-menu, anchored under the ProjectSwitcher (anchorRef). It is an anchored dropdown, not an Overlay and not a MenuPanel. screens.title: Sheets
screens.purpose: A modal question card (sheet) dropped over the dimmed main window to ask one question and take one answer: confirm a destructive action, or prompt for a name with Cancel and an accept verb. It is rendered by SheetHost from the sheetStore's current spec and resolves to accept, instead or dismiss.

regions.name: Scrim (Backdrop)
regions.contents: Full-window fixed layer, 1180x760 in all five states, dim soft (bg-black/30, measured oklab(0 0 0 / 0.3)), no blur, z-modal, fades in with animate-scrim-in. Sits over the main-window screen, which stays visible but dimmed. A press outside the card dismisses (via Overlay, not read).

regions.name: Card (Sheet surface)
regions.contents: Centred dialog, role=dialog, aria-modal, width min(26rem,100%) = 364px in every recorded state, radius 10.5px. Height 141px for new-list, new-project and rename-list (at 408,309); 122px for delete-list and delete-confirm (at 408,319, has a detail line). Animates in with animate-sheet-in.

regions.name: Header row (glyph badge + headline)
regions.contents: Flex row, centred vertically, gap-space-6. Holds the 32px tinted glyph badge (glyph box 423,324 on name sheets, 423,334 on confirm sheets) and the h2 headline at x 455 (Label, font-display, 15px, semibold, wraps).

regions.name: Detail line
regions.contents: Optional one-line secondary paragraph under the header row (Label as p, 12.5px, mt-space-6). Present only in delete-list and delete-confirm. Measured box 418,366 345x19.

regions.name: Field area
regions.contents: Optional body under the text block (div mt-space-7, min-w-0), box 418,359 345x35 for the InputWell. Present only when the spec has an ask: an InputWell with a text input and, when dice is set, a roll IconButton (trailing slot). screens.title: Attachment lightbox
screens.purpose: Full-window lightbox over the dimmed main window that previews one attachment of the selected task at a large size, steps through the task's other attachments, and offers open, reveal, rename and remove for that attachment. It is closed by the close button, Escape, or a click on the empty stage.

regions.name: scrim (Backdrop2)
regions.contents: Full-window 1180x760 dim/blur layer rendered by Overlay (layer overlay, dim strong, blur) over the main window. Visually a dark grey; exact colour not measured (B, estimated). Whether a bare click on the scrim closes the lightbox is unconfirmed (Overlay source not read by either).

regions.name: backdrop (main window, not part of this screen)
regions.contents: Dimmed main window behind the scrim: window controls, Spring switcher, list tabs Website and Press kit, New list, Split view, Hide preview panel, Settings, task search, task row Rewrite the hero section (1 of 2 subtasks, Attachments count 2), footer Sort & filter, 1 / 5 done, 20 %, and the task inspector with Notes, Subtasks and Attachments. Not interactive while the lightbox is open.

regions.name: top bar
regions.contents: Row across the top holding the file-kind icon, the file name, an optional position counter, and five BarButtons. Clicks here do not close (stopPropagation). Code: h-13 (52px), px-space-7, gap-space-4. Measured (B): about 40px tall (y 0 to 40), controls 28px at y 9, no fill or border. The measured values are used for look; see notes for the height conflict.

regions.name: stage
regions.contents: flex-1 area below the top bar (relative flex min-h-0 items-center justify-center px-16 pb-8). Empty space closes the lightbox. Holds the chevrons and the media wrapper. Measured (B): the image is centred at approx x 350 to 830, y 239 to 539 in shot.png.

regions.name: chevrons
regions.contents: Previous and Next buttons absolutely positioned at the left and right edges of the stage, rendered only when there is more than one attachment. Measured (B): Previous at [14,370,39,39] and Next at [1128,370,39,39], at the vertical middle of the stage.

regions.name: media
regions.contents: Centred wrapper (flex max-h-full max-w-full items-center justify-center) that stops propagation and renders one body branch: Loading, the fallback card, image, video, audio, PDF embed, or text.

regions.name: keyboard
regions.contents: Window-level capture keydown handler for ArrowLeft and ArrowRight, plus Escape via Overlay captureEscape.

catalogue.title: Buttons
catalogue.description: Buttons in the Taskscape desktop task-manager app: title-bar icon toggles, project switcher, footer and grid bulk actions, inspector and rich-text editor buttons, sheet and dialog buttons, toast, trash, settings and capture-bar controls, plus key-actions, including the click-activated shortcut recorder. Built from the 95 row objects of rows-buttons.json (kinds: button, toolbar-button, key-action; no row uses kind link). The source count of 96 could not be reconciled with the file, so a row may be missing between rows 37 and 52 and is not catalogued here.

catalogue.title: Icon buttons
catalogue.description: Icon-only buttons across the Taskscape screens: window traffic lights and Windows/Linux window controls, list tab and project controls, search-bar and row action buttons, toolbar buttons, inspector header actions, filter panel, lightbox, settings and trash controls. The 93 source rows are grouped into 50 variants by look and behaviour; widgets that act differently are kept apart (for example, the inert traffic lights and the close, minimise and full-screen lights).

variants.name: Traffic light, close, enabled
variants.description: Red macOS window traffic light that closes the window (or the Settings window). Rows: title-bar close, main-window close (same disc as the title-bar row, bundled in the main-window row), settings-capture close, settings-about close. The main-window row and the title-bar row are the same control on different screens.
variants.look: 14x14 disc (title-bar box 14x14 at 18,15); button size-4 (16px) containing svg viewBox 85.4; lit ring #e24b41, fill #ed6a5f, glyph #460804; glyph X fades in on hover. The oklch(0.26 0.012 262) value recorded in the main-window and Trash rows is not used for this glyph: it sits beside font settings and is probably the text colour (unverified).
states: unlit when window blurred (inactive colours, no glyph)
variants.behaviour: Click closes the window. Title-bar calls win.close() (WindowControls.tsx:139). Disabled only if the action is missing.

catalogue.title: Selection and toggles
catalogue.description: Selection and toggle widgets of the Taskscape desktop task manager: list tabs in the title bar and inspectors, round task checkboxes and row-select toggles, small square checkboxes, segmented controls, the settings switch, and the settings sidebar tabs. All 39 rows in rows-choice.json are assigned to exactly one of the 13 variants below.

variants.name: list tab, active (label)
variants.component: Label (list tab name, active); ListTabs > Label on draft-inspector; ? on multi-inspector, filter-panel, trash
variants.description: The labelled name of the open list, shown in primary tone with a medium weight. Covers rows 1 (main-window), 8 (draft-inspector), 12 (multi-inspector), 19 (filter-panel) and 22 (trash, combined row that also lists the inactive tabs; assigned here because a row can land in only one variant). Multi-inspector and filter-panel record a close x button on the active tab (x 280 on filter-panel); main-window and draft-inspector do not record one. Whether the other screens' tabs carry a close button is not recorded. Row 12 refers to a 'see close entry' that does not exist in rows-choice.json; the close button is therefore described in this variant's look field as a sub-element.
variants.look: Text box 51x20 at 224,12; font 500 13px/19.5px; truncate; max-w-40; text-[13px]. tracking-[0.01em] is recorded on main-window (row 1 and row 2); draft-inspector (rows 8 and 9) lists no tracking, so it is either omitted there or not recorded. Colour oklch(0.26 0.012 262) light / oklch(0.94 0.004 260) dark. Tab sits in a hairline frame about x 211-308 (rows 4 and 19; shot estimate). Row 1 records 212-309 instead; this 1 px difference is unresolved and may be a shot-estimate artefact. Close button sub-element (multi-inspector and filter-panel only): an x button on the active tab, at x 280 on filter-panel; its own size and colour are not recorded.
states: split-view: blue pane marker before the name, text moves to x 249 (main-window)
variants.behaviour: Click selects the list (handler not in these files; inferred). On multi-inspector, click keeps this list open (switching not recorded); close via its x button.

variants.name: list tab, inactive (label)
variants.component: Label (list tab name, inactive); ListTabs > Label on draft-inspector; ? on multi-inspector, filter-panel
variants.description: The labelled name of another list in muted tone, shown beside the active tab. Covers rows 2 (main-window), 9 (draft-inspector), 13 (multi-inspector) and 20 (filter-panel). Trash is listed in usedIn because its inactive Reading and Garden tabs share this look; those tabs are recorded only inside row 22, which is assigned to the active variant, so they are not counted as separate rows here. Thin vertical separators sit between tabs on several screens.
variants.look: Font 500 13px/19.5px, truncate, max-w-40, text-[13px]. Colour oklch(0.62 0.013 264) light / oklch(0.57 0.011 262) dark. Label boxes: Reading at 322,12 (54x20), Garden at 422,12 (48x20).

variants.description: The full, interactive list tab in the title bar (row 4 only). It is a container around the list name with focus, hover, drag and inline-rename states, and a delete button on its right side. This is the richest form of the list tab and behaves differently from the label-only variants, so it is kept separate.

Its accessible label is Select and it reads aria-pressed=false, which is the row selection state, not completion. Row 3 wires both onToggleDone and onToggleSelect, so this may overlap the row select toggle variant; that merge is unverified. Row 10 count is unresolved: the row records 8 draft-inspector tasks, but its states list 7 unchecked rows plus 2 checked rows (t-post, t-milk), which totals 9. Do not rely on the 8 figure until rows-choice.json is reconciled. Rows 21 and 23 record the kind as round-check; row 3 and row 10 record it as checkbox.

The inventory has no select rows, so no select variants are listed.

catalogue.title: Menus
catalogue.description: Menus are the family of floating or inline choice surfaces in the Taskscape desktop app: the project switcher pill and its project list, anchored popovers, right-click context menus with their rows and submenus, option menus opened from buttons, the command palette rows, and the mention autocomplete. The formatting floating toolbar is a strip of formatting buttons rather than a choice list; it is kept in this family only because the source groups it with the floating surfaces. The 29 source rows (from spec/inventory/rows-menus.json) group into 21 variants. Every row is in exactly one variant. Rows with no measured look (look null or "Not measured") are described from their component and text only, and the item notes say so. Kind vocabulary: 'context-menu' marks a menu opened at the cursor or by right-click; 'menu' marks a menu opened from a control such as a button or the search bar; 'menu-item' marks a single row; 'popover' and 'dropdown' mark anchored panels.

It is anchored with anchorRef and onDismiss and is neither an Overlay nor a MenuPanel. Its row contents are in the two project-row variants. usedIn lists the capture screens only (title-bar and context-menus); the source does not say the panel is absent from the other screens that show the pill.

variants.name: task row context menu
variants.description: The menu opened from right-click or the More button on a task row. It has two content sets, kept in this one variant because the source records them as one row with one open menu. The single-row set holds Copy, Add subtask, Rename, Move to list, Promote to top level (only when the task has a parent_id) and Delete task…. The multi-row set is used when two or more rows are selected and this row is one of them; it holds Copy {n} tasks, Mark {n} done, Mark {n} not done and Delete {n} tasks…, with no Rename and no Add subtask.
variants.look: Not measured (look null in the source row). Items use the same MenuItem rows as the other menus (icon + label). Dividers sit above 'Add subtask', above 'Mark {n} done' and above 'Delete task…' (and above 'Delete {n} tasks…' in the multi-row set). 'Promote to top level' appears only when the task has a parent_id.
variants.behaviour: Each item runs its action: copy to clipboard, mark done or not done, add subtask (sets the inline composer), rename (beginTitleEdit), promote, delete (requestDeleteTask for one row or bulkDelete for many), or move. 'Move to list' is disabled when there are no other lists and opens a submenu of list names with id move:{listId}.

Where two rows looked alike but differed in a measured or behavioural way, they were kept apart.
